sentences.text:
Coram:
 Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Anup Jairam Bhambhani
 Order

Pursuant to what was recorded in last order dated 27.03.2023, the petitioner has filed the present application seeking to implead co- accused Rehmat as petitioner No.2 in the present quashing petition.
2. Petitioner No.2 has filed an affidavit in support of the application and is also present in court.

3. Since the matter is at its initial stages and the impleadment is necessary in view of what was recorded in the last order, it is not considered necessary to issue notice on the application.
4.
The application is therefore, allowed.
Petitioner No.2 is impleaded as a party in the matter.
5. Amended memo of parties filed, is taken on record.
6. The application is disposed-of.

7. By way of the present petition filed under section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure 1973, the petitioners and complainant/respondent No. 2, jointly seek quashing of case FIR No.0030/2022 dated 28.07.2022 registered under sections 419/420 of the Indian Penal Code 1860 ('IPC' for short)
at P.S.: Cyber Police Station North East.
8. The petition is supported by affidavits of the petitioners, as also of respondents No.2, alongwith proofs of their I.Ds.

sentences.text: Petitioner No.1's father, petitioner No.2 and respondent No.2 are present in court in-person.

Their credentials have been verified and they have also been identified by their respective counsel.
10.
Petitioner No.1 is stated to be in judicial custody in the present case.

He is accordingly represented in court by his father (Tajuddin), who is also a signatory to the Settlement Deed dated 15.11.2022, whereby the matter has been compromised and settled with respondent No.2, who (latter) is present in court today.
11. The court has interacted with respondent No.2.

He confirms that he has received the amount of Rs.1,35,000/-as the settlement amount, and includes the money that was stated to have been drawn from his accounts by the petitioners; and he does not wish to pursue any further proceedings in the FIR.

12. The court has interacted with petitioner No.1's father as also with petitioner No.2 and respondent No.2, who have confirmed that they have now resolved the matter and Settlement Deed dated 15.11.2022 has been signed by them closing all issues amicably.
Parties now wish to live in peace and harmony going forward.
13. Mr. Shoaib Haider, learned APP submits that the State has no objection to the FIR being quashed.

14. In the circumstances, in line with the law laid down by the Supreme Court in Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab & Anr. reported as (2012) 10 SCC 303 as also in Narinder Singh & Ors. vs. State of Punjab & Anr. reported as (2014) 6 SCC 466, this court sees no reason why the subject FIR and all proceedings emanating therefrom should not be quashed.

sentences.text: This court is of the view that in light of the settlement between the contesting parties, continuing with the subject FIR and all subsequent proceedings would be an exercise in futility and would not be conducive to peace and harmony between the parties.
15. Accordingly, FIR No.0030/2022 dated 28.07.2022 registered under sections 419/420 IPC at P.S.: Cyber Police Station North East is quashed.
All proceedings arising therefrom also stand closed.
16. Petition stands disposed of.

17. Pending applications, if any, also stand disposed-of.
18.
The date of 10th August 2023, given earlier stands cancelled.
ANUP JAIRAM BHAMBHANI, J APRIL 21, 2023/
